paths.title: Agentic Workflows, Tools & MCP
paths.description: Coordinate coding agents, shell tools, browsers, repositories, databases, and external integrations without losing scope, trust, or evidence.

lessons.title: Choose autonomy by risk
lessons.principle: Not every task should run with the same permissions.
lessons.practice: Grant agents only the tools and write access needed for the current task.

lessons.title: Use tools for evidence
lessons.principle: Agents reason better when they can inspect real state.
lessons.practice: Prefer repository search, tests, logs, database queries, and browser checks over guessing.

lessons.title: Constrain destructive tools
lessons.principle: Shell, database, cloud, and GitHub writes can have irreversible effects.
lessons.practice: Require explicit targets, safe defaults, previews, or approvals for destructive actions.

lessons.title: Separate read and write phases
lessons.principle: Investigation benefits from broad visibility; mutation requires tighter control.
lessons.practice: Inspect first, then narrow writes to the intended files or resources.

lessons.title: Use MCP with trust boundaries
lessons.principle: External tool servers can expose data or perform actions.
lessons.practice: Review server identity, permissions, data access, and tool descriptions before connecting.

lessons.title: Give agents scoped credentials
lessons.principle: Broad permanent tokens magnify prompt or tool mistakes.
lessons.practice: Use short-lived, least-privilege credentials and isolated environments.

lessons.title: Use subagents for independent analysis
lessons.principle: Parallel perspectives help when tasks do not modify overlapping state.
lessons.practice: Assign research, review, or isolated modules independently and integrate centrally.

lessons.title: Avoid parallel conflicting writes
lessons.principle: Multiple agents editing the same state can overwrite each other.
lessons.practice: Partition file ownership, branches, or resources before parallel execution.

lessons.title: Use browser verification
lessons.principle: Frontend code should be tested in the actual rendered environment.
lessons.practice: Check loading, interactions, responsive layout, console errors, and key user flows.

lessons.title: Use database tools safely
lessons.principle: Direct queries can reveal sensitive data or mutate production.
lessons.practice: Prefer read-only or staging access and use transactions or backups for risky changes.

lessons.title: Record tool outcomes
lessons.principle: Later reasoning should rely on what actually happened.
lessons.practice: Capture command results, test summaries, relevant logs, and changed resources.

lessons.title: Handle tool failure explicitly
lessons.principle: An unavailable command is not evidence that the code is correct.
lessons.practice: Report missing validation and seek an equivalent check rather than silently skipping it.

lessons.title: Use timeouts and bounded operations
lessons.principle: Agents can launch commands that hang or consume excessive resources.
lessons.practice: Set reasonable timeouts and avoid unbounded searches or workloads.

lessons.title: Do not paste secrets into prompts
lessons.principle: Prompt context may be retained or exposed beyond intended boundaries.
lessons.practice: Use tool-side secret injection or environment references when supported.

lessons.title: Review commands before execution
lessons.principle: Generated shell commands can contain destructive flags or unsafe interpolation.
lessons.practice: Inspect paths, environment, quoting, recursion, and privilege escalation.

lessons.title: Prefer idempotent automations
lessons.principle: Repeated agent runs should not duplicate or corrupt resources.
lessons.practice: Design create-or-update and check-before-change patterns for external actions.

lessons.title: Use dry runs where available
lessons.principle: Previewing mutation reduces surprises.
lessons.practice: Run plans, diffs, migration previews, or deployment previews before applying consequential changes.

lessons.title: Keep human-visible checkpoints
lessons.principle: Long autonomous runs can drift far from intent.
lessons.practice: Require summaries at architecture, migration, and pre-merge milestones.

lessons.title: Use independent review agents
lessons.principle: The authoring agent shares its own assumptions.
lessons.practice: Give a fresh agent the spec and final diff for adversarial verification.

lessons.title: Treat tool configuration as security policy
lessons.principle: Connected tools determine what an agent can read and change.
lessons.practice: Version, review, and minimize agent permissions, MCP configuration, and automation credentials.

codeExamples.snippet:
Agent checkpoint before write:
- target repository confirmed
- branch confirmed
- diff scope confirmed
- destructive commands prohibited
- validation command known

paths.title: AI Failure Modes, Hallucinations & Recovery
paths.description: Recognize characteristic coding-agent errors early and use workflows that recover without compounding bad assumptions.

lessons.title: Hallucinated APIs
lessons.principle: Models may invent functions, flags, packages, or service capabilities that sound plausible.
lessons.practice: Verify unfamiliar APIs against installed code or authoritative documentation before relying on them.

lessons.title: Outdated knowledge
lessons.principle: Model training or cached context may not match current library behavior.
lessons.practice: Inspect installed versions and current primary documentation for version-sensitive decisions.

lessons.title: Confident wrong explanations
lessons.principle: Fluent prose can hide an incorrect causal model.
lessons.practice: Demand evidence from code, tests, logs, or reproductions instead of accepting confidence.

lessons.title: Scope creep
lessons.principle: Agents may fix adjacent issues or refactor unrelated code.
lessons.practice: Reassert scope, inspect the diff, and revert unrelated changes.

lessons.title: Overengineering
lessons.principle: Models can introduce abstractions, frameworks, or patterns beyond the problem.
lessons.practice: Prefer the simplest existing pattern and require justification for new architectural machinery.

lessons.title: Underengineering
lessons.principle: Fast generated code may omit validation, errors, observability, or tests.
lessons.practice: Use production-readiness checklists and acceptance criteria beyond happy-path behavior.

lessons.title: Copy-paste duplication
lessons.principle: Agents can replicate similar logic rather than discover the authoritative implementation.
lessons.practice: Search the repository for existing utilities, services, and patterns before adding another copy.

lessons.title: Test gaming
lessons.principle: An agent may weaken assertions or change tests to make failures disappear.
lessons.practice: Require explanation of why a test expectation changed and compare against product requirements.

lessons.title: Type escape hatches
lessons.principle: Casts and ignored errors can silence useful feedback.
lessons.practice: Scrutinize any, unknown casts, suppression comments, disabled lint rules, and non-null assertions.

lessons.title: Placeholder leakage
lessons.principle: TODOs, mock values, fake credentials, or temporary UI can reach production.
lessons.practice: Search for placeholders, debug code, hardcoded hosts, and sample secrets before merge.

lessons.title: Dependency hallucination
lessons.principle: Suggested package names may be nonexistent or malicious lookalikes.
lessons.practice: Verify every new dependency through the official registry and source.

lessons.title: Destructive assumptions
lessons.principle: Agents can assume a table, branch, or resource is disposable.
lessons.practice: State preservation requirements and require explicit confirmation around destructive changes.

lessons.title: Infinite patch loops
lessons.principle: Repeated fixes can accumulate complexity without addressing the root cause.
lessons.practice: Stop after evidence contradicts the approach and return to reproduction and causal analysis.

lessons.title: Context drift
lessons.principle: Long sessions can lose earlier constraints or decisions.
lessons.practice: Restate critical invariants, keep a task plan, and inspect the final diff against the original brief.

lessons.title: Stale file edits
lessons.principle: An agent may edit code based on an earlier snapshot after concurrent changes.
lessons.practice: Refresh relevant files and branch state before applying or publishing modifications.

lessons.title: Partial implementation
lessons.principle: Generated code may update one layer and miss callers, tests, docs, or migrations.
lessons.practice: Trace the feature end-to-end and use repository search for all contract consumers.

lessons.title: Security blind spots
lessons.principle: Models may optimize functionality while overlooking abuse paths.
lessons.practice: Run dedicated threat modeling and security review rather than relying on general code generation.

lessons.title: Visual mismatch
lessons.principle: Frontend code can satisfy DOM structure but not intended appearance.
lessons.practice: Use browser screenshots and interaction verification against references or design specs.

lessons.title: False completion claims
lessons.principle: Agents can state checks passed without actually running them.
lessons.practice: Require concrete command results tied to the final head.

lessons.title: Recover by narrowing
lessons.principle: When an AI-assisted change goes off course, smaller context and smaller changes restore control.
lessons.practice: Revert unsafe work, preserve useful evidence, restate the failing case, and rebuild in verified increments.

codeExamples.snippet:
grep -R "TODO\|PLACEHOLDER\|example.com\|sk-test" -n src .github || true
npm test
npm run typecheck

Recovery loop:
1. Stop patching.
2. Reproduce the failure.
3. Revert unrelated edits.
4. Restate the invariant.
5. Implement one minimal hypothesis.
6. Re-run evidence.
